tldr: Headlines globally converge on the same factual event — the G7 will release 100 million barrels — but diverge sharply on causation: anglophone and Asian outlets append 'after Trump threat' or 'after US pressure' to announcements that wire services and most continental European outlets present as a cooperative G7 act. The US conservative Daily Wire alone frames this as a Trump political victory, while Germany's ZDF is the only outlet whose headline adds expert scepticism that prices will only fall briefly.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Only headline to frame the outcome as a Trump victory narrative rather than a cooperative policy response — 'Trump Put The Squeeze On Europe. It Worked.' — signalling US conservative media's emphasis on coercive leverage over multilateral diplomacy.

Only headline in the corpus that adds expert skepticism: 'Expertin: G7-Reserven senken Spritpreise nur kurzfristig' (expert says reserves only lower fuel prices short-term). All other outlets present the release as a solution; this headline frames it as an insufficient one.

RT's headline — 'US threatens Europe with diesel export ban' — focuses entirely on the US coercion phase before the agreement was reached, absent any mention of the G7 deal itself. The framing positions the US as an aggressor toward Europe rather than a coordinator.

Only headline to provide cumulative context: the G7 had promised 400 million barrels in March, 325 million have already been released, making the new 100 million an incremental top-up. No other outlet's title signals this, leaving most readers with an inflated sense of the decision's novelty.

bottom_line: Headline coverage projects factual consensus on the event while embedding a coercion subtext in roughly half the corpus — outlets across the UK, Asia-Pacific, Germany, and the Nordic countries attach US pressure/threat language that wire services and most continental outlets omit, making the headline layer's dominant story not the G7 release itself but Washington's arm-twisting to produce it.
